title: Three-Color DFS Cycle Detection
description: Interactive vis-network visualization demonstrating the three-color DFS algorithm for detecting cycles in directed graphs, specifically for validating learning graph DAG structure
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: algorithms
graph theory
cycle detection
depth-first search
learning graphs
DAG validation

controls.navigation_buttons: Zoom and pan the network view
controls.legend: Shows the three colors (White, Gray, Black) and their meanings
controls.stack_display: Shows the current DFS traversal stack
controls.cycle_alert: Highlights when a cycle is detected with explanation

learningObjectives: Identify the meaning of the White (unvisited), Gray (on the DFS stack), and Black (fully explored) node states
Explain why an edge pointing to a Gray node is a back edge that proves a cycle exists
Trace the DFS stack as it grows and shrinks, noting where each node is recolored Gray then Black
Predict whether a given directed graph is a DAG by locating back edges such as Recursion to Loops
Explain why a learning graph must be acyclic, using the Loops-requires-Recursion deadlock as a counterexample
Calculate the O(V + E) time and O(V) space cost of three-color DFS cycle detection
